title: VC versus PC when Compliance Falls
subtitle: Compare airway pressure and delivered volume responses when respiratory compliance changes under volume control

patient.summary: Intubated patient with acute lung injury mechanically ventilated under deep sedation.

options.label: Switch to PC-AC (Pinsp 10, PEEP 5) at compliance 25 mL/cmH2O

prediction.question: When respiratory system compliance decreases from 50 to 25 mL/cmH2O in volume-control mode (VC-AC, VT 500 mL), how will peak airway pressure (Ppeak), plateau pressure (Pplat), and delivered expiratory tidal volume (VTe) change?

whatToLookAtHint: Monitor peak inspiratory pressure, plateau pressure, and delivered tidal volume on the ventilator display.

reflection.question: In volume-control ventilation (VC-AC), why does falling compliance cause plateau pressure to rise while tidal volume remains unchanged?

options.text: VC mode guarantees delivered volume by cycling on volume, so alveolar elastic recoil pressure (VT / C) must rise when compliance drops.
The ventilator increases flow rate automatically to overcome lower chest wall stiffness.
VC mode regulates peak airway pressure at a constant level by reducing expiratory time.
Falling compliance reduces airway resistance, allowing higher alveolar pressures.

reflection.explanation: Volume control fixes the inspiratory flow waveform and delivered tidal volume. According to the equation of motion, alveolar plateau pressure is Pplat = PEEP + VT / C. When compliance falls by half (from 50 to 25 mL/cmH2O), the elastic driving pressure required to distend the lung with the same 500 mL tidal volume doubles (from 10 to 20 cmH2O). In contrast, pressure control (PC-AC) fixes the inspiratory pressure, meaning falling compliance causes delivered tidal volume to drop while pressure remains constant.

evidence.claim: In volume-controlled ventilation, delivered tidal volume is constant while peak and plateau pressures vary with respiratory system compliance; in pressure-controlled ventilation, pressure is fixed and volume varies.
evidence.source: Chatburn RL, Volsko TA. Mechanical ventilation: modern concepts and practice. In: Hess DR, et al., eds. Respiratory Care: Principles and Practice. 4th ed. Jones & Bartlett; 2021.

evidence.claim: Driving pressure (Pplat - PEEP) is inversely proportional to respiratory system compliance at a fixed tidal volume.
evidence.source: Amato MB, et al. Driving pressure and survival in the acute respiratory distress syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2015;372(8):747-755.
